editorial_contributions.text: Summary: In this paper, we prove a fixed point theorem for contractive mapping of integral type in complete metric spaces by using iterative approximations. This paper extends and improves results of Rakotch (1962), Branciari (2002), and several other results announced by many authors. An example and few remarks are given to show that our result is a proper extension of existing ones.

title.title: Making an \(H\)-free graph \(k\)-colorable

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: For an element \(r\) of a ring \(R\), a \(D(r)m\)-tuple is an \(m\)-tuple \((a_1,\ldots a_m)\) of elements of \(R\) such that for all \(i,j\) with \(i\neq j, a_ia_j+r\) is a perfect square in \(R\). In this article, we compute and estimate the measures of the sets of \(D(r)m\)-tuples in the ring \(\mathbb{Z}_p\) of \(p\)-adic integers, as well as in its residue field \(\mathbb{F}_p\).

editorial_contributions.text:
[For the entire collection see Zbl 0544.00026.] 


This paper is a review paper on optimal control and optimization of mechanical system dynamics. Based on a great experience in modern design of mechanical systems, the authors proposed a general procedure (named the adjoint variable method) for the calculation of design sensitivities (i.e. first and second derivatives of the performance index of mechanical system). The applications of this procedure are discussed by comparison with the direct differentiation method for systems described by first order differential equations and by second order differential and algebraic equations. Many illustrative examples (design of oscillators, design sensitivity analysis of a burst fire automatic cannon, vehicle suspension dynamic optimization a.s.o) and a short description of algorithms proposed for computation of design sensitivities point out the validity and numerical efficiency of the adjoint variable method.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: In this paper, we have derived common fixed point results for weakly compatible self mappings satisfying E.A. property in fuzzy metric spaces. As consequences of our results we obtain some corollaries. Finally, we give an example and some applications to integral type contractions to verify the effectiveness and applicability of our main results.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: The purpose of this paper is to obtain some results on existence of fixed points for contractive mappings in fuzzy metric spaces using control function. We prove our results on fuzzy metric spaces in the sense of George and Veeramani. Our results mainly generalize and extend the result of Grabeic (1988). As an application, a consequence theorem of integral type contraction is given in support of our result.

editorial_contributions.text:
Summary: \textsc{Candy Nim} is a variant of \textsc{Nim} in which both players aim to take the last candy in a game of \textsc{Nim}, with the added simultaneous secondary goal of taking as many candies as possible. We give bounds on the number of candies the first and second players obtain in 3-pile \(\mathcal{P}\) positions as well as strategies that are provably optimal for some families of such games. We also show how to construct a game with \(N\) candies such that the loser takes the largest possible number of candies and how to bound the number of candies the winner can take in an arbitrary \(\mathcal{P}\) position with \(N\) total candies.

For the entire collection see [Zbl 1572.91002].

Navier Stokes equations are employed to obtain the flow field, and the components of velocity for primary and secondary flow, stream function are obtained. Further, two particular cases are deduced and discussed for the radius of cavity. Finally, Equi-pressure lines, streamlines, and vortex lines are constructed to visually demonstrate the impact of different factors on the flow pattern.

editorial_contributions.text: Single degree of freedom plane linkages (formed of rigid bars with unfettered joints) must consist of \(\geq 4\) bars. There are a few linkages of 5 and 6 bars that allow motions not executable by the 4-bar linkage. The condition of one degree of freedom imposes a determinant condition on the motions of these linkages. The authors note that modern symbolic computation programs can solve these equations in closed form: the condition that given 5 or 6 dimensional determinants with complex coefficients vanish splits into two real polynomial equations whose common root can be found by Sylvester's dialytical method from a linear equation. The corresponding computations are quite hopeless for hand calculation. Sylvester's resultant naturally still has to be solved numerically as polynomial equation of high degree (with the accompanying danger of ill conditioning, making a big question whether practical engineering can really gain from these computations as compared to the usual trial and error approximations).

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: The aim of this paper is to introduce the sufficient condition for the existence and uniqueness of common fixed points for pair of self-maps satisfying a generalized \(\int\limits_{\varphi}^{\psi}\) weakly contractive condition involving \(C\)-class functions in the setting of complete metric spaces. Our results extends and improve many recent results in the literature. As application of our results, we obtain several interesting consequence results of fixed point theorems. Example and remarks are also given to justify the importance and usability of our results.
